title: Rhode Island Holiday Guide
intro: Holiday shows, concerts, lights, Santa, markets and church bazaars across Rhode Island, from early November through New Year’s Day, with times, places and prices.

items.note: Trinity Rep’s annual A Christmas Carol returns to the Dowling Theater at 201 Washington Street in Providence for its 50th-anniversary production, with the run continuing through December 31. Dickens’s story follows Ebenezer Scrooge through the Christmas encounters that change his view of the people around him. Choose a specific date and showtime through Trinity Rep’s ticket calendar.

items.t: 'Twas the Night Before... by Cirque du Soleil
items.note: Acrobatics, dance and Christmas music bring a familiar holiday poem to the stage when Cirque du Soleil presents ’Twas the Night Before… at PPAC in Providence. The family production combines its Christmas characters and story with the company’s physical performance style, offering a holiday outing built around movement and spectacle. PPAC advertises a family-ticket offer involving a child age 18 or younger and a regularly priced ticket; check the box office for the current terms and available seats.

items.t: Sara Evans: Holiday Road Tour with Braden Hull
items.where: The Historic Park Theatre & Event Center
items.note: Sara Evans brings her holiday tour to Cranston.

items.t: Vienna Boys Choir: Christmas in Vienna
items.where: The Historic Park Theatre & Event Center
items.note: The Vienna Boys Choir performs its Christmas program.

items.t: Boston Pops Holiday Concert with Keith Lockhart
items.note: Keith Lockhart and the Boston Pops bring their holiday concert to PPAC in Providence, with a program that includes “Sleigh Ride,” seasonal arrangements and a sing-along. A visit from Santa is part of the festivities, giving the orchestral concert a family element alongside its music. There are afternoon and evening performances on the same day, so check the selected showtime carefully when reserving seats through PPAC.

items.where: The Historic Park Theatre & Event Center
items.note: Irish music and dance celebrate Christmas traditions.

Clara’s Christmas Eve adventure unfolds to Tchaikovsky’s score when Ballet Rhode Island performs The Nutcracker at The VETS in Providence. Company artists share the stage with local young performers in the holiday ballet, bringing together its Christmas story, classical dancing and familiar music. Tickets are listed from $36 through the company’s official ticket providers. Selected matinees offer a post-show “Meet the Stars” experience; check whether it is attached to this performance when booking.

items.t: Disney On Ice: Magic in the Stars
items.note: Frozen 2, Moana, Encanto, Toy Story and more on ice, with no Christmas Day show.

Rosecliff becomes part of the performance when Newport Contemporary Ballet presents The Newport Nutcracker. Rather than keeping the entire audience in a conventional theater setting, the production moves through the mansion and includes a Newport-themed second act, connecting the ballet’s holiday story with the city around it. Admission is for ages 6 and older, with tickets listed from $159.
The Arctic Playhouse stages Dickens’s story of Ebenezer Scrooge and the supernatural visitors who force him to reconsider his life.
The unruly Herdmans transform a Christmas pageant.
Scrooge rediscovers compassion through ghostly encounters.
The Stadium Theatre’s adaptation of A Christmas Carol follows Ebenezer Scrooge through the visits that challenge his isolation and reshape his understanding of Christmas.

The low voices of Cantus fill Emmanuel Church in Newport with Christmas music on December 5 at 3:30 p.m. The concert pairs familiar carols with contemporary choral works, offering listeners both recognizable seasonal melodies and newer music written for voices. Its focus is the ensemble’s singing and the holiday repertoire, making this an afternoon option for readers looking for a concert rather than a market or outdoor festival. See Newport Classical for tickets and seating information.
Handel’s Messiah in the Rosecliff ballroom, sung by Ensemble Altera and the Professional Choristers of the Choir School of Newport County.

Providence College’s Chorus and Liturgical Choir lead Advent Lessons and Carols at St. Dominic Chapel on December 6, from 4 to 5:15 p.m. The service brings seasonal readings and choral music into a chapel setting, with the music forming part of the observance of Advent. Hot chocolate and cookies follow, extending the gathering beyond the service itself. Check the college or diocesan announcement for visiting information before arriving on campus.

items.t: Ocean State Pops Orchestra: Holiday Pops
items.note: The orchestra presents a holiday pops concert.

items.t: The Irish Tenors: A Family Christmas
items.note: The Irish Tenors bring their family Christmas show to Washington Square.

Frisson brings a chamber-music Christmas program to Emmanuel Church in Newport. Selections from The Nutcracker and Vivaldi’s Winter share the program with “Carol of the Bells” and a Christmas sing-along, moving between classical concert music and familiar seasonal favorites. Two performances are listed that afternoon. Check Newport Classical’s booking calendar for the 1:00 p.m. performance before purchasing, since the linked series page may open on another seating.

items.t: Westerly Band Holiday Concert: Tribute to America and the Holidays
items.note: The Westerly Band presents “Tribute to America and the Holidays” at the Westerly Armory on December 13 at 2:00 p.m. The concert brings the community band into a seasonal setting, with its title joining a patriotic theme to the holiday program. Readers looking for an afternoon performance can check the band or armory announcement for the repertoire, admission and seating arrangements before attending.
items.price: $8 suggested donation for adults; children free

items.note: The Rhode Island Philharmonic and the Providence Singers, conducted by Christine Noel, in a Sunday matinee of Handel’s Messiah.
items.addr: The VETS, 1 Avenue of the Arts, Providence

items.where: Cathedral of Saints Peter and Paul
items.note: Christmas and Advent music serves a local cause when the Gregorian Concert Choir and Festival Orchestra perform “The Sounds of the Season” at Providence’s Cathedral of Saints Peter and Paul on December 13 at 3:00 p.m. Proceeds benefit the Diocese of Providence’s Keep the Heat On program, which helps households facing heating costs. Tickets are listed at $20, making the concert an opportunity to hear the choir and orchestra while supporting heating assistance.

items.t: Very Merry Dickens Carolers at Island Cemetery and Belmont Chapel
items.note: A seasonal caroling appearance; the listing does not give a time.

items.t: A Musical Retelling of ‘A Christmas Carol’ with Christine Baranski
items.note: One night only: the vocal ensemble Skylark sings the story, narrated by actress Christine Baranski.

The Chorus of Westerly presents Christmas Pops at George Kent Performance Hall, bringing old and new holiday favorites together in its seasonal concert. The program is built around Christmas music performed by the chorus, giving audiences a chance to hear familiar repertoire in a live choral setting. Performances are listed on both December 19 and 20; consult the chorus’s current ticket calendar to confirm the time and available seats for this date.

items.t: A Christmas Carol, read by Michael Langlois
items.note: Dickens’s Christmas story takes the form of a theatrical reading when Michael Langlois presents A Christmas Carol in Blithewold Manor’s Dining Room in Bristol on December 20 at 6:30 p.m. The performance offers a spoken interpretation of the story within the mansion’s holiday setting, rather than a full theater production. Readers planning a visit should reserve for the reading itself and check whether admission to other Blithewold holiday attractions is included or sold separately.

Sparkling Lights at The Breakers pairs a half-mile outdoor light walk with a visit inside the decorated Newport mansion. The experience runs on selected evenings from November 21 through December 27, with listed hours of 4 to 8 p.m, allowing visitors to see both the grounds and the house during the same outing. Admission is ticketed, and the season dates do not mean it operates every night. Select an available date and timed entry before traveling.

Blithewold Manor in Bristol welcomes visitors into its decorated rooms for Christmas at Blithewold, with the season running November 24 through January 3. The mansion’s holiday setting can be paired with an evening visit to Sparkle!, the grounds’ light display, subject to separate schedules and ticket arrangements. Listed mansion hours are Tuesday through Sunday, 11 a.m. to 7 p.m, with Thanksgiving and Christmas closures. Check the booking calendar before selecting a date.

Pawtucket’s Centreville Bank Stadium becomes a holiday destination for the Rhode Island Lights Festival, with light displays, a makers village, entertainment and visits from Santa. The season runs November 27 through January 3 at 11 Tidewater Street, with evening hours of 5 to 10 p.m.; the later schedule excludes December 24 and 25. Food and seasonal refreshments are part of the experience. Check the festival’s ticket calendar for admission and any changes to operating dates.

Decorated boats take their holiday displays onto Newport Harbor for the Illuminated Boat Parade on November 27 at 6:00 p.m. Crews compete for the best display, turning the harbor itself into the setting for the evening’s celebration. The event is listed as free to watch, giving visitors an outdoor holiday option along the Newport waterfront. Check the organizer’s latest announcement for viewing guidance and weather-related changes before making the trip.

The Lewis Family Light Show turns 12 Shenandoah Road in Warwick into a synchronized holiday display, with visitors listening to the accompanying music on 106.9 FM from their cars. The season runs November 27 through December 31, with hours varying by day of the week. The display is free, and donations support The Autism Project. Check the family’s posted schedule for the evening you plan to visit and follow its viewing guidance.

Garden City Center’s holiday lighting celebration brings community activities to Cranston on November 28, from 2 to 6 p.m. Visitors can take part in a community art project benefiting Adoption Rhode Island, explore samples and join the seasonal gathering before Santa’s expected arrival in a vintage car around 4:30 p.m. The afternoon combines shopping-center festivities with a charitable project and a family visit from Santa. See the organizer’s schedule for the final activity lineup.

Santa joins a free holiday gathering at the Shops at Long Wharf in Newport on November 28, from 4 to 6 p.m. The program includes a tree lighting, music, children’s crafts, letters to Santa and photo opportunities, bringing several family activities into a single late-afternoon visit. The rain date is November 29, which is an alternative date rather than a second scheduled celebration. Check the organizer’s announcement if the forecast affects the event.

Newport Harbor Island Resort celebrates its Lighting of the Lighthouse on November 28 at 5:00 p.m, with carolers and seasonal decorations accompanying the public gathering. Hot chocolate for children and cider are included in the event description, adding refreshments to the waterfront holiday tradition. The lighthouse lighting offers an early-evening stop for visitors already exploring Newport’s seasonal celebrations; confirm the resort’s latest event arrangements before arriving.
Explore illuminated holiday displays.

Wickford begins its 41st annual Festival of Lights with the official tree lighting at Updike Park. The opening brings the village into a four-day holiday program that continues through December 6 with shopping, music and family activities. Visitors can make the tree lighting their first stop in the village celebration, but should check the organizer’s final schedule for the ceremony time and other opening-night activities.
The campus glows with 1,000 luminarias.

Richmond’s annual Christmas tree lighting is listed for December 4, bringing a community holiday gathering to the town’s December calendar. The announcement establishes the date but does not provide the venue, starting time or a complete activity program. Check the Ocean Community Chamber or town announcement before making plans, particularly if coordinating the lighting with another holiday outing that evening.

South Kingstown’s Festival of Trees brings decorated trees together with seasonal activities during a December 4–January 3 run. The listing describes children’s activities, caroling, music, cocoa and handmade local gifts, combining things to see with opportunities to shop and gather. Confirm the venue and operating calendar with the organizer.

items.t: Coventry Winter Wonderland Craft Fair and Tree Lighting
items.note: Coventry’s Winter Wonderland and Tree Lighting brings a day of holiday activities to the Guy Lefebvre Community Center on Saturday, December 5. The town’s October 30 report confirms craft vendors, food trucks, free pictures with Santa and activities from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m, followed by a tree-lighting celebration from 5:30 to 6:30 p.m. The daytime program gives families time to browse and visit Santa before returning or staying for the evening lighting. Check Parks and Recreation for weather arrangements and the final activity schedule.

Bowen’s Wharf celebrates its 56th annual Christmas tree lighting in Newport on December 5, with festivities beginning around 12:30 p.m. and the tree illuminated at 6 p.m. Santa, live music, local musicians and choruses fill the afternoon program before the evening lighting. Santa and Mrs. Claus are expected to arrive by boat if the weather allows, adding a harbor arrival to the wharf’s celebration. Admission is free; check the organizer’s program for the final sequence of activities.

Slater Park’s Winter Wonderland welcomes visitors in Pawtucket, with decorated trees, a miniature village and a talking snowman. The program also lists carousel and train rides, horse-drawn hayrides, Santa visits, face painting and children’s crafts, mixing a walk through the displays with activities for families. Opening night on December 5 includes the mayor’s tree lighting and Santa arriving by fire truck. Check the city’s current announcement for individual attraction availability and any separate ride arrangements.

Providence’s City Hall tree-lighting celebration fills the downtown holiday schedule on December 5, from 4 to 7 p.m, at 25 Dorrance Street. Community choirs, live bands and family activities join Santa’s parade into downtown, with food trucks and an ice-skating DJ party also included in the festival descriptions. The event sits within the wider Providence Holiday Festival weekend, allowing families to combine the tree-lighting festivities with the nearby market and skating.

WaterFire’s Holiday Basin Lighting brings an evening gathering to Providence on December 11, with the illuminated basin forming the center of the seasonal event. This is the December holiday lighting on WaterFire’s calendar, distinct from its New Year’s Eve program at the pedestrian bridge. Consult the organizer’s event page for the lighting ceremony, public hours and any additional activities before heading downtown.
Decorated trees glow along the walkway.
A three-hour outing with a train ride, the story, hot chocolate and Santa.

items.t: Seasonal skating at The Providence Rink
items.note: The Providence Rink adds an outdoor skating option to the downtown holiday season, with public sessions and bumper-car experiences listed on its calendar. A rink visit can be paired with the surrounding holiday festivities, but skating hours and ticket arrangements vary by session.

items.t: Ice Theatre of New York at The Providence Rink
items.note: Ice Theatre of New York brings a performance to The Providence Rink, giving downtown holiday visitors a chance to watch professional skating without buying a show ticket. The free appearance is part of an evening that includes two performances and a public skating dance party with a local DJ afterward. Visitors who want to skate themselves should check the rink’s admission, rental and session arrangements separately from the free performance.

items.t: Santa and Mrs. Claus Arrive by Boat
items.note: Welcome Santa and Mrs. Claus at the wharf before their fire-truck ride to the Conanicut Gift Shop.

Cookies, Cocoa, & Claus brings a family holiday gathering to Westerly on December 5. The announcement confirms the date, but the venue and detailed schedule are still needed before a visit can be planned.
Families visit Santa in a sensory-friendly setting.
A family holiday tea includes a special guest and photos; a waitlist is available.
Participants build and decorate a gingerbread animal exhibit.
Carol singing and a Christmas reading accompany Santa's visit.

Santa joins passengers aboard the Coastal Queen for a Newport meet-and-greet cruise. The approximately one-hour outing combines time with Santa, hot chocolate and holiday music aboard a decorated boat, taking a familiar seasonal visit onto the water. Confirm the departure point, ticket availability and any weather-related arrangements with the cruise operator.

items.t: Christmas Pageant at St. Francis Church
items.note: Children’s Christmas storytelling takes a parish form when St. Francis Church in Wakefield holds its Christmas Pageant on December 20 at 10:00 a.m, following the 9 a.m. Mass. The pageant is part of the church’s seasonal program rather than a separately described theatrical production. Check with the parish for visitor arrangements and whether families should attend Mass first or arrive for the pageant itself.
A hands-on Winter Wonder Workshop to make a snowman ornament.

items.t: Garden City Center Holiday Farmers Market
items.note: Garden City Center’s Holiday Farmers Market brings a seasonal pop-up shopping experience to Cranston in partnership with Rhode Island Night Market. The listing gives November 15–22 as the date span, offering a way to browse holiday vendors alongside a visit to the center’s shops. That span does not establish daily operation, so check the organizer’s individual market dates, hours and participating vendors before choosing a day.

items.t: Holiday Sip & Shop at Mount Hope Farm
items.note: An evening of holiday shopping at the farm.

Downtown Bristol begins its holiday-shopping season with the Holiday Preview on November 20, when participating shops extend their hours for an evening of browsing. The event offers an early opportunity to explore the downtown businesses before December’s larger tree-lighting and market celebrations. The announcement does not give a complete schedule or list of participating stores, so check with the downtown organizers or individual businesses for that evening’s hours.

items.time: Sat 10 AM–4 PM; Sun 11 AM–3 PM
items.note: The Rhode Island Christmas Festival fills the West Warwick Civic Center with an indoor holiday-shopping program. The event offers another way to browse seasonal vendors without relying on an outdoor village market, with the organizer’s final lineup determining the mix of gifts, crafts and activities. Check the festival page for admission, hours and participating vendors before heading to the civic center; the dates cover November 21 and 22.
Author Lisa Goddard signs her children’s holiday book.

The Good Trade Makers Market returns to WaterFire Arts Center in Providence, bringing independent makers together for its sixth year. The description says about half of the participating businesses are Rhode Island-based, connecting the wider market with local shopping. Visitors can browse handmade work and meet the people behind it rather than choosing from a single retailer’s stock. Check the organizer’s page for hours, admission and the full participant list.

Christmas decorations fill The Breakers, Marble House and Chateau-sur-Mer during Holidays at the Newport Mansions, whose season runs November 21 through January 3. Trees, wreaths, flowers and period table settings give each house a seasonal presentation within its historic rooms. Visitors can plan a mansion visit during the day and consider the separately ticketed Sparkling Lights experience at The Breakers on selected evenings. Consult the Preservation Society’s calendar for house hours, admission and holiday closures.

items.t: Christmas Preparations with the 1910 Household Staff
items.note: Costumed household staff show how the manor got ready for a 1910 Christmas, then you tour the decorated house on your own.
items.more: Two timed sessions; check Blithewold for tickets.

items.note: A visit with Santa, co-hosted with Lorelei’s for Littles.
items.more: Time not listed; check before you go.

items.note: Blithewold’s holiday charcuterie workshop turns seasonal entertaining into a hands-on subject on November 23 in Bristol. Led by the mansion’s private-events manager, the program focuses on charcuterie skills for holiday gatherings, offering an activity beyond touring the decorated house. Reserve through Blithewold and check the current workshop description for the session time, price, materials and anything participants should bring.

Winter Afternoon Tea invites visitors to pause in Blithewold’s holiday setting in Bristol, with the schedule covering Tuesdays through Fridays from November 24 to December 18. Seatings begin at 11 a.m, and reservations are made for particular dates rather than the season as a whole. The tea offers a seated gathering within the mansion alongside the wider Christmas program. Consult the booking page for available seatings, the menu, prices and holiday exceptions.

items.t: A Rough Point Holiday: After Dark
items.note: Doris Duke’s oceanfront house decorated for the season and open after dark, with warm drinks and jazz.

items.t: Holiday Jazz Tea with Chelley Knight’s Quartet
items.note: Live jazz with afternoon tea in the manor dining room.

The German American Cultural Society of Rhode Island hosts Christkindlmarkt in Pawtucket on November 28, from noon to 5 p.m. More than 25 local artisans are listed, offering pottery, ornaments, gifts, soaps, jewelry, textiles, wreaths and holiday greens. The mix makes the market a place to look for handmade presents and seasonal decorations in the same visit. Consult the society’s announcement for admission information and any changes to the vendor program.

The Fez-tival of Trees opens at Rhodes on the Pawtuxet in Cranston on November 28, combining a holiday tree display with a market. Visitors can make the decorated trees the focus of the outing and browse the accompanying holiday offerings during the same visit.
A holiday brunch with Santa on Goat Island.

Newport’s Christmas Doorway Competition brings holiday decorating into the community’s own entrances and streets, with Discover Newport inviting participation in the 2026 program. The competition adds a neighborhood-scale tradition to a calendar otherwise filled with concerts, lights and markets.

Downtown Westerly’s Holiday Stroll and Luminaria begins at 5 p.m. on December 2, bringing seasonal activity into the downtown streets. Luminaria and opportunities for Santa photos form part of the program, making the evening a chance to combine a walk through the celebration with a family holiday stop. Check the organizer’s current map and schedule for the participating locations and Santa photo arrangements.
Make a holiday wreath with Blithewold’s horticulture team.
items.more: Check Blithewold for supplies and price.

items.note: Chepachet’s Candlelight Shopping fills Main Street and the roundabout with holiday activity. The program includes a 6 p.m. tree lighting at Kent Field, Santa and Mrs. Claus photos, children’s crafts at Manton Library and dinner at Chepachet Union Church. Local caroling also includes an open-mic invitation, giving community members a chance to sing as well as listen while exploring the village’s shops.

items.time: Thu–Fri 5–9 PM; Sat noon–8; Sun noon–5
items.note: Local makers, food and seasonal entertainment bring holiday shopping outdoors when the PVD Downcity Holiday Market opens at Grant’s Block Park and Westminster Street in Providence. The market combines browsing with family activities and pop-up performances, giving visitors reasons to stay downtown beyond a single shopping stop. It is part of the December 3–6 Providence Holiday Festival, whose other attractions include the city tree lighting, skating and an illuminated stroll.
items.addr: Grant’s Block Park and Westminster St., Providence

items.t: Wreath Decorating Workshop at Mount Hope Farm
items.note: An evening wreath-decorating workshop in the farm’s barn.
items.more: Confirm price and registration with the farm.

items.where: Pawtucket Armory Center for the Arts
items.note: Artists sell handmade holiday gifts.

Providence’s December 3–6 Holiday Festival brings several downtown traditions into one weekend: a makers market, the City Hall tree lighting, skating, workshops and live entertainment. Trolley service is also included in the festival description, helping connect parts of the program. The umbrella festival is listed here on its opening date, December 3; individual activities appear separately under their own dates and times. Check the organizer’s program as additional details are announced.
A multi-faith gathering with music, dance and prayers reflecting traditions of light and themes of mercy and care for the Earth.
Holiday shopping inside the historic Colony House.

items.where: Biltmore Park and Providence Rink to Grant's Block
items.note: A lighted procession brings music and movement through downtown Providence on December 4 at 6:00 p.m, when Illuminate PVD’s Holiday Stroll heads toward the Downcity Holiday Market. The Providence Drum Troupe and pop-up performers lead the route from the Biltmore Park and Providence Rink area toward Grant’s Block Park. The walk connects the festival’s downtown gathering places, allowing visitors to follow the procession and continue into the market’s food, makers and seasonal activities.
An advance shopping evening before the main market.
A holiday evening at the historic house, catered by Russell Morin. Check the organizer for admission and age requirements.
Village shops and craft fairs celebrate the season, with Santa arriving by boat at 1 PM.
Make a fresh wreath with the Preservation Society’s greenhouse staff.
Live music, dance and festive lighting animate Federal Hill.

items.t: Bristol Christmas Festival and European Market
items.note: Bristol’s Christmas Festival and European Market begins December 5, bringing vendor huts, holiday food, crafts and entertainment into the downtown celebration. The program describes stage and street performances, Santa, wreath decorating and children’s crafts, giving families activities alongside the shopping. This listing marks the opening date, December 5; the full sequence of market days and hours still needs confirmation through the organizer’s calendar.

Bristol gathers for its Grand Illumination on December 5 near the Burnside Building at Hope and Court streets, where the town’s Christmas tree lighting anchors the celebration. Local school performers and other holiday festivities are part of the program, connecting the downtown decorations with a community gathering. The rain date is December 6. Check the town’s final announcement for the program’s start time and any weather-related move to the alternate date.

The Intentional Celebration: Holiday Edition brings an indoor makers market and seasonal activities to WaterFire Arts Center in Providence. The program includes local makers, food trucks, music, children’s activities and Santa, combining shopping with a family outing. A separate VIP early-access hour is also advertised. Check the organizer’s booking page for general-entry hours, the VIP option and the day’s activity schedule before selecting tickets.
Holiday shopping from local makers.

Whitehall Museum House in Middletown opens for a colonial-style Christmas gathering on December 6, from 1 to 3 p.m. Decorations, live music and a traditional wassail bowl form part of the afternoon, with festive treats prepared by the Colonial Dames. The program offers a smaller historic-house celebration, centered on seasonal customs and hospitality rather than a large commercial light display. See the event announcement for visitor and admission information.

Glen Manor House opens its doors for its Christmas Open House on December 6, from 1:30 to 4 p.m. The visit offers an opportunity to see the house dressed for the holidays during a seasonal public opening, rather than attending a private function there. Check Glen Manor’s own announcement for admission arrangements and any visitor instructions, especially if combining the afternoon with another East Bay holiday stop.
A morning tour of how the mansions are decorated for the holidays.

items.where: West Glocester Fire Station to Ponaganset High School
items.note: Glocester’s Christmas Parade begins at 6 p.m. on December 11, following a route through Chepachet and beyond. The procession starts at West Glocester Fire Station, travels east on Route 44 through the village, then follows Sawmill Road and Snake Hill Road toward Ponaganset High School. Residents and visitors should choose a viewing point along the announced route and check the organizer’s latest notice for traffic arrangements or weather changes.

items.t: Christmas Open House at the Irish Museum
items.note: The Museum of Newport Irish History holds its 10th annual Christmas Open House on December 12, offering a seasonal visit to the museum during Newport’s holiday program. The event combines the museum setting with a Christmas gathering, providing an alternative to the larger outdoor festivals and performances. Check the museum’s announcement for opening hours, admission and the ornament details mentioned in the listing before planning a stop.

items.t: Pictures with Santa and ‘A Visit from St. Nicholas’
items.note: Photos with Santa, with readings of the poem at noon, 12:30 and 1, plus a Spanish-language reading at 1:30.

items.t: Music in the Living Room at Blithewold
items.note: Holiday music in the decorated manor: mezzo-soprano Nancy Hood on Dec 12 and jazz pianist Laszlo Gardony on Dec 13.
items.price: Ticket includes manor and grounds admission
items.more: Registration required to reserve a seat.

items.t: Holiday Cruises with the Dickens Carolers from Newport
items.note: 75-minute caroling cruises on the Coastal Queen.
items.price: $44 adults; $39 seniors and military; $34 children and youth

items.note: A holiday-season author event.
A seasonal flower-arranging workshop.

St. Anthony Church in North Providence holds its 35th annual Holiday Bazaar, raising money for the parish’s Religious Education Program. The bazaar offers a parish gathering within the early holiday-shopping season. The two-day bazaar continues Sunday, November 8, when a parish breakfast and a visit from Santa are also listed. Consult the church’s announcement for the sale offerings, raffle arrangements and any updates before attending.

St. Thomas Church in Providence hosts its Christmas Bazaar on November 7, from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m, with crafts, baked goods, raffles and games. Food is part of the draw, including the pastor’s pierogis, giving visitors a reason to stay beyond browsing the sale tables. The full-day schedule offers flexibility for an early holiday-shopping stop; check the parish announcement for the final program and any individual raffle or food-service times.

items.t: Greek Food Fair and Christmas Bazaar
items.note: The Church of the Annunciation in Cranston hosts its Greek Food Fair and Christmas Bazaar, bringing food and holiday browsing into the same parish gathering. Greek dishes, pastries and coffee join crafts, raffles and a white elephant sale, with proceeds supporting the Philoptochos Society’s charitable work.

St. Raymond’s Church Hall in Providence opens for its Christmas Bazaar, with free entry and a mix of holiday shopping and parish food offerings. Visitors can browse crafts, knitted goods, wreaths, greenery and a boutique, alongside baked goods, hot food, raffles and a penny social. The dates cover both November 7 and 8; confirm the hours for this day with the parish before planning a visit.
items.addr: Parish hall, North Main St., Providence

items.t: St. Vincent de Paul Harvest Bazaar
items.note: Homemade crafts, baked goods, jewelry, a basket raffle, grocery bingo and roll-up tables.
items.addr: 6 St. Vincent de Paul St., Coventry

items.note: Holy Trinity Church in Woonsocket holds its annual Christmas Bazaar on November 14, from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Handmade crafts and baked goods share the program with a penny social, raffles and a lunch kitchen, while children’s crafts and photos with Santa add family activities. The gathering combines parish fundraising with a chance to shop and eat during the same visit. Check the church’s current announcement for any activity-specific times.

St. Robert Bellarmine Church in Johnston hosts its Holiday Bazaar on November 14, with vendor tables, food and fundraising activities supporting the parish food shelf and outreach ministries. A silent auction, raffles and a straw game are included in the program, offering ways to participate beyond shopping. Check the parish or diocesan calendar for the public hours and the timing of individual activities before visiting the church hall.

items.t: St. Cecilia Church Hall Christmas Bazaar
items.time: Fri 9 AM–8 PM; Sat 9 AM–2 PM
items.note: Food, raffles, a silent auction, books, crafts, tools, plants and vendors, from St. John Paul II Parish.
items.more: Saturday ticket sales end at 1:30 p.m.

items.note: St. Theresa Church Hall in Burrillville presents The Wonder of Christmas Bazaar, from noon to 7 p.m. The parish program includes bingo, raffles, food and a penny social, bringing several fundraising activities into its two-day holiday gathering. Missy Ducharme leads Friday caroling from 5 to 6:30 p.m. Check the parish announcement for the complete activity schedule and any separate arrangements for games or food service.
items.addr: St. Theresa’s Shrine hall, 35 Dion Drive, Nasonville

items.t: St. Francis of Assisi Holiday Bazaar
items.note: St. Francis of Assisi in Wakefield holds its Holiday Bazaar on November 21, from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. Crafters and vendors join a silent auction, bake sale and café, giving visitors a mix of holiday shopping and refreshments while supporting the parish. The morning and early-afternoon schedule makes it an option before later holiday outings; see the parish or diocesan announcement for any updates to the program.
items.addr: Father Greenan Center, 114 High St., Wakefield

items.t: Phillips Memorial Baptist Church Holiday Bazaar
items.note: Handmade gifts, baked goods and family activities.

items.t: St. Martin de Porres Center Holiday Bazaar
items.note: Handmade crafts, home décor, holiday items and gifts. Open to all.

items.t: Seniors’ Christmas Party with Bishop Lewandowski
items.note: Food, fellowship and holiday cheer for seniors. All are welcome.

items.t: Nine Lessons and Carols: Christmas on the Hill
items.note: Trinity Church and its Choir School sing the traditional service of lessons and carols.

items.t: Christmas Lessons and Carols with Choral Holy Eucharist
items.note: The church’s choirs lead this seasonal liturgy.

items.t: Christmas Eve Choral Eucharist with String Quartet
items.note: A festive Eucharist follows prelude music beginning at 9:00 PM.
Families make their own hanukkiah, with PJ Library and Harbor Creative Arts.
items.price: $18 per family, kit included; extra kits $18

items.where: Jewish Alliance of Greater Rhode Island
items.note: A Hanukkah shopping pop-up.
items.more: Check the Alliance calendar for place and hours.

sections.label: New Year’s Eve and New Year’s Day

items.t: Noon Year’s Eve at Providence Children’s Museum
items.note: Performances, paper crowns and a confetti countdown at noon.
items.more: Confirm this year’s date and tickets with the museum.

items.t: Countdown to Noon Year at MobileQuest
items.note: MobileQuest’s “Countdown to Noon Year” is listed in Cranston for December 31, from 10 a.m. to noon, with STEM activities and a daytime countdown. Check the venue’s current announcement for the confirmed 2026 schedule, ticket price and available places before booking a family visit.

items.t: Noon New Year’s Eve Party with the Trolls
items.note: A family skating party, with optional climbing or laser tag.

items.t: Noon Year’s Eve at Warwick Public Library
items.note: Warwick Public Library gives families an early way to welcome the year with its Noon Year’s Eve Party on December 31, from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. Crafts, music, snacks and activities lead into a noon countdown in the Children’s Library, with adults and children attending together. The listing describes a dress-up theme and free admission; check the library’s event page for branch details, registration and any final instructions.

items.t: Noon Year’s Eve at North Providence Union Free Library
items.note: A craft program and countdown for younger children.
items.more: Registration required; confirm with the library.

items.t: Kids Noon Year’s Eve at Kingston Free Library
items.note: Kingston Free Library welcomes families to Kids Noon Year’s Eve on December 31, from noon to 2 p.m, in Potter Hall in South Kingstown. Crafts, games and free play accompany a noon balloon drop, allowing preschoolers and school-age children to celebrate without staying up late. The library says no food will be served, so plan snacks separately. Consult the event page for registration and other visitor instructions.
Two-hour bowling reservations with lights and music; food available.

A Charlestown New Year’s Eve bonfire at Ninigret Park, 5 Park Lane, is listed for December 31. The only source we found is a December 2025 announcement for a Wednesday, December 31 bonfire at 5 p.m., so the 2026 date and time are unconfirmed. The gathering centers on a community bonfire, offering an outdoor early-evening alternative to a late-night dinner or party. The page does not establish admission, age restrictions or a fuller program. Confirm the town or organizer’s current announcement, including weather arrangements, before heading to the park.

items.t: Providence New Year’s Eve Celebration and Illuminate PVD Fireworks
items.where: 195 District Park and the Van Leesten Pedestrian Bridge
items.note: Providence’s New Year’s Eve celebration brings music, food and family activities to 195 District Park and the Michael Van Leesten Memorial Pedestrian Bridge on December 31, from 5 to 9 p.m. The free, all-ages gathering combines entertainment and illuminated installations before an 8:30 p.m. fireworks show over the river.

items.t: Holiday Lights Spectacular on New Year’s Eve
items.note: Roger Williams Park Zoo’s Holiday Lights Spectacular welcomes New Year’s Eve visitors on December 31, from 5 to 9:30 p.m, at 1000 Elmwood Avenue in Providence. The walking route covers 40 acres and is described as featuring more than 3.5 million lights, making the displays the focus of the evening visit. Advance online tickets are required; a later listing gives a $13–$15 range. Confirm the price for the selected entry time when booking.

Gracie’s welcomes New Year’s Eve diners with “An Evening in Bloom” at 194 Washington Street in Providence on December 31. The listing begins at 5 p.m. and offers a choice of five- or seven-course seasonal tasting menus, with wine pairings available. The meal puts the evening’s focus on a sequence of dishes rather than a separately described entertainment program. Reserve directly and confirm the menu price, seating time and pairing options.

Claudine’s early New Year’s Eve seating offers a five-course chef’s tasting menu, with the seating concluding at 7:30. The price is $155 per person before beverages, tax and gratuity, giving diners a defined early-evening meal before other plans. Reserve the early seating specifically and check the restaurant’s current menu and cancellation arrangements when booking.

items.t: Warwick New Year’s Eve at Rocky Point
items.note: Food trucks, music, giveaways for kids and early fireworks.
items.more: The city hasn’t posted this year’s page yet; confirm with Warwick before going.

items.t: New Year’s Eve Mass in ASL, English and Spanish
items.note: St. Patrick Church at 244 Smith Street in Providence lists a New Year’s Eve Mass interpreted in ASL, English and Spanish on December 31 at 6 p.m. The service offers a worship option within the evening’s celebrations, with interpretation central to the announcement. Check the Diocese of Providence’s current Christmas and New Year schedule or contact the parish to confirm the service arrangements before attending.

items.t: Weekapaug Inn New Year’s Eve Dinner
items.note: Weekapaug Inn’s first New Year’s Eve dinner seating begins at 6 p.m. Spray Rock Road in Westerly. The five-course meal is paired with live music in the Sea Room, with an optional wine pairing for diners who want it.

The Chanler’s “The Scarlet House” combines a crimson-themed reception with dinner and dancing on December 31, from 7 p.m. to 1 a.m, at 117 Memorial Boulevard in Newport. Live modern violin leads into a four-course meal, followed by a DJ, late-night bites and a midnight toast. The price is $385 plus service charge and tax. Reserve directly and confirm the current menu, dress guidance and total price.

items.t: The Dancing Feeling Ballroom New Year’s Eve
items.note: The Dancing Feeling brings ballroom dancing to Rhodes on the Pawtuxet in Cranston on December 31, beginning at 7 p.m. Hors d’oeuvres and a buffet accompany continuous dancing, with a professional American Rhythm dance show adding a performance segment to the evening. A midnight toast is included, and dancing continues until 12:30 a.m. Check the organizer’s current ticket options, dress guidance and admission arrangements before reserving.

items.t: Little Miss and The Boom at The Blue Room
items.note: Little Miss and The Boom bring swing, blues, jazz and rockabilly to The Blue Room at 2200 Broad Street in Cranston on December 31. The listing gives a 7:30 p.m. time, putting the band into the early part of the evening’s celebrations. Ticket and dinner details were still forthcoming, so check the venue’s current announcement before planning a meal or assuming a particular admission package.

items.t: Newport Harbor Island Resort New Year’s Eve
items.note: Newport Harbor Island Resort has announced a New Year’s Eve celebration on Goat Island for December 31, from 8:30 p.m. to 1 a.m. Check the resort’s updated event page before booking so that the ticket inclusions, dining arrangements and program are clear, rather than assuming a particular band or dinner format.

items.t: Ocean House ‘London Calling’ New Year’s Eve Ball
items.note: Ocean House’s “London Calling” New Year’s Eve Ball gives the Seaside Ballroom a 1960s British theme on December 31, from 9 p.m. to 1 a.m. A DJ, dancing, food stations, a photo set and costume prizes form the program, making dressing for the theme part of the evening’s entertainment. Tickets are listed at $275 for guests 21 and older and $175 for those under 21; confirm booking terms and the current program.

Crosswind brings a Chris Stapleton tribute to Chan’s Egg Rolls & Jazz at 267 Main Street in Woonsocket on December 31. Doors open at 7:30 p.m, with the show listed from 9 p.m. to midnight; a dance floor, hats, noisemakers and a midnight toast join the music. Admission is listed at $50, with an optional $30 buffet before tax and tip. Confirm whether the buffet and concert require separate reservations.

items.t: Cross’ Mills Library Noon Year’s Eve
items.note: Make hats and noisemakers, play games, sing karaoke, and watch the ball drop at noon.
items.more: Register by phone. Last year it ran 11 to noon; confirm this year’s time.

items.t: A Christmas Carol: New Year’s Eve performance
items.note: The final day of Trinity Rep’s 50th-anniversary Christmas Carol.

items.t: Providence Zen Center New Year’s Eve Practice
items.note: Providence Zen Center’s New Year retreat in Cumberland begins December 30 and includes a New Year’s Eve practice program at 99 Pound Road. The description mentions a Sangha dinner, evening practice, midnight practice and an overnight stay for participants, offering a contemplative way to cross into the year. The registration covers multiple days, so confirm the exact December 31 schedule, accommodation arrangements and available places with the center.

items.t: Mass at St. Gregory the Great
items.where: St. Gregory the Great, 360 Cowesett Road
items.note: St. Gregory the Great Church lists daily Mass at 8:30 a.m. on December 31 at 360 Cowesett Road in Warwick. The morning service provides a worship option before the evening’s New Year celebrations. Confirm the parish’s current holiday calendar before attending, particularly if looking for an additional vigil service rather than the morning Mass described in this listing.

items.t: Lewis Family Christmas Light Show: last night
items.note: No charge; tune to 106.9 FM for the music.

items.t: Bilingual New Year’s Eve Mass, St. Michael the Archangel
items.note: St. Michael the Archangel Church in Providence is included as a possible New Year’s Eve worship option, but the source is a December 2025 bulletin. That bulletin lists a bilingual December 31 Mass at 6 p.m.; it does not confirm the December 31, 2026 service. Contact the parish for this year’s holiday schedule before planning attendance or publishing the older time as current.

Newport Playhouse lists a December 31 performance of Social Security, a comedy in which a family visit disrupts a couple’s quiet life. The announcement also says the theater plans to close on December 31, 2026, making it especially important to check the venue’s current status and available seats.

items.t: Down City Band at the Narragansett Cafe
items.note: Down City Band brings live music to the Narragansett Cafe in Jamestown on December 31, with the performance scheduled from 8:30 to 11:59 p.m. The band gives the evening a local music focus for visitors spending New Year’s Eve on the island. Admission, reservations and age restrictions are not established in the listing, so check directly with the cafe before organizing dinner or a group around the performance.

A Wish Come True’s 23rd Annual Polar Plunge Challenge brings “Freezin’ for a Reason” to Easton’s Beach in Newport on January 1. The plunge begins at noon sharp at 175 Memorial Boulevard, with a listed event window extending to 1:30 p.m. Spectators are welcome as well as participants, and participation begins with a $25 donation. Register through the organizer and check its arrival instructions before heading to the beach.

items.t: First Day Hike at Goddard Memorial State Park
items.where: Goddard Memorial State Park, 1095 Ives Road
items.note: Rhode Island State Parks’ First Day Hike page describes a previous January 1 outing at Goddard Memorial State Park in Warwick, with a 1.5-mile loop and a 10 a.m.–1 p.m. program. It does not establish a January 1, 2027 hike, so those details remain an example from a prior year rather than a confirmed invitation. Check the parks department’s new-year announcement for the 2027 location, hours and registration arrangements.

items.where: Goddard State Park Beach, 1095 Ives Road
items.note: MENTOR Rhode Island’s Frozen Clam Dip and Obsta-Plunge gives New Year’s Day participants a choice of a cold-water plunge, a ninja-style obstacle course or both. The January 1 event runs from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Goddard State Park Beach, 1095 Ives Road in Warwick. The page points to organizer ticketing without establishing a price; check the registration options, participation requirements and arrival instructions before signing up.

items.t: Holiday Lights Spectacular on New Year’s Day
items.where: Roger Williams Park Zoo, 1000 Elmwood Ave.
items.note: Roger Williams Park Zoo’s Holiday Lights Spectacular continues on New Year’s Day, January 1, from 5 to 9:30 p.m. at 1000 Elmwood Avenue in Providence. Visitors follow a walking route through the holiday displays, offering an evening outing after the daytime New Year’s celebrations. The listing gives advance online tickets at $13–$15; confirm the price and available entry slots when booking.

items.t: New Year’s Day Mass, St. Michael the Archangel
items.note: Bilingual Mass listed in the December 2025 bulletin; confirm the 2027 time.
